explanation: Her windscreen (windshield) wiper swept a rubber blade across the glass when the driver turned a lever inside. The patent ran out in 1920, before wipers became common.

claims.text: Mary Anderson received a US patent for a windscreen (windshield) wiper in 1903.
Mary Anderson did not patent snow chains, a car heater or a rear-view mirror.
Anderson was inspired during a streetcar ride in New York in snowy weather, when the driver struggled to see.
Her device swept a rubber blade across the glass when a lever inside the vehicle was turned.
Anderson's patent expired in 1920, before windscreen wipers became common on cars.

evidence.restatement: Mary Anderson was granted a US patent for a hand-operated windscreen wiper in November 1903.
Anderson's one famous patent is the wiper; she is not credited with snow chains, a car heater or a rear-view mirror.
The New York streetcar story is the standard biographical anecdote, but I know of no primary record of it, so I treat it as tradition rather than documented fact.

evidence.restatement: Her device used a lever inside the vehicle to sweep a rubber blade across the glass.
A US patent of 1903 ran 17 years, so hers lapsed in 1920. Whether wipers were not yet common by then is vague, since they were widely fitted by the early 1920s.
